title: Comparison of allogeneic and autogenous bone grafts for augmentation of alveolar ridge defects – a 12-month retrospective radiographic evaluation
authors: Kloss FR, Offermanns V, Kloss-Brandstätter A. Clin Oral Implants Res. 2018 Nov;29(11):1163-1175.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss maxgraft blocks (processed human allograft) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Freeze-dried cancellous allogeneic bone blocks showed equivalent volumetric shrinkage rates as autogenous bone blocks when used for treating circumscribed bone defects classified as Type- II to Type-IV according to the ITI-treatment guide categories. Therefore, it is not necessary to over-contour the alveolar ridge when using allogeneic blocks for treating single tooth defects, but to apply the same procedure as when using autogenous blocks” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
